misconceptions.description: Believing printed text travels through the auditory/verbal channel because its content is verbal, so pairing an animation with on-screen text is treated as balancing the two channels.
misconceptions.trigger: learner pairs an animation with simultaneous on-screen text and assumes the two channels are balanced
misconceptions.feedback: Printed text enters through the eyes, so it loads the visual channel alongside the picture or animation, and the two compete for the same limited capacity. Route the explanation to spoken narration so the verbal stream travels through the idle auditory channel.

misconceptions.description: Assuming working memory can hold an arbitrary number of elements, so adding more on-screen content always helps.
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds detail or elements to a screen to be thorough and ignores capacity limits
misconceptions.feedback: Working memory processes only a few elements at once. Segment dense material and let the learner control pacing so the number of interacting elements stays within capacity.

misconceptions.description: Treating mere dual presentation of words and pictures as proof of learning, ignoring the active selecting, organizing, and integrating the learner must do.
misconceptions.trigger: learner justifies a screen only by saying it shows both pictures and words
misconceptions.feedback: Dual presentation is necessary but not sufficient. Show how the design prompts the learner to select, organize, and integrate the material into a coherent model.

misconceptions.description: Treating productive difficulty as removable clutter: seeing a prediction prompt or self-explanation step as extraneous load and deleting it to 'reduce load.'
misconceptions.trigger: learner strips a prediction or self-explanation prompt during a load-reduction revision and reports the frame as improved
misconceptions.feedback: Germane processing is difficulty you protect, not noise you remove. Cutting the prediction prompt lowers the felt effort but removes the schema-building work the frame existed to provoke. Reduce extraneous load (redundant text, decoration), and keep the prompts that make the learner select, organize, and integrate.
